findings.cross_file_justification: The new refusal subclasses ConfigError, which cmd_invoke's fallback walker treats as a hard abort. Under prefer-cli, the resolver places this adapter before the Google HTTP hop.
findings.description: With agy_opt_in absent or false, Google invocations using prefer-cli now terminate at the first CLI hop even when a configured, authenticated HTTP fallback is available. The planners described in the reviewer context exclude the voice only under cli-only, so prefer-cli still schedules an invocation that this new default refusal aborts.
findings.failure_mode: The invocation returns INVALID_CONFIG without attempting the HTTP fallback, causing an otherwise usable Google voice to fail and reviews to become degraded.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude the agy hop during chain resolution when opt-in is disabled, allowing prefer-cli to continue through HTTP routes. Keep an explicit opt-in refusal for direct agy or cli-only requests with no permitted route.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new refusal is raised from the diff-touched adapter's complete() and typed as ConfigError in the diff-touched types.py; the consumer is cheval's unchanged chain walker, which hard-aborts on ConfigError (STATIC misconfig arm, cheval.py ~2545). The cheval.py hunks in this diff touch only the effort path, so no skip-on-opt_in_required branch was added.
findings.description: AgyOptInRequiredError subclasses ConfigError. cheval's fallback-chain walker treats ConfigError as a static misconfig and hard-aborts the whole chain instead of walking to the next hop. With the new default (opt-in off), any Google chain that places the gemini-headless hop first (hounfour.headless.mode: prefer-cli, or a catalog chain whose terminal is gemini-headless) now aborts at that hop with INVALID_CONFIG before the gemini-api HTTP rung is ever tried. The adapter docstring and the error docstring both claim the seam reads as 'not planned, never a failed voice', but the only thing honoring that is the shell/TS planners (flatline-orchestrator.sh, bridgebuilder config.ts) which, per the reviewer notes, treat only `cli-only` as agy-routed; adversarial-review.sh filters only the companion chain, not the primary model+fallback_chain. So a planner plans the voice, cheval refuses it, and the run records a failed/DEGRADED voice: the exact outcome FR-1 is meant to prevent.
findings.failure_mode: On a default install (opt-in absent) with a Google model routed prefer-cli, `cheval invoke` exits INVALID_CONFIG on the agy hop with the HTTP fallback untried; review orchestrators record a failed hop / DEGRADED council rather than skipping the voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) have the chain walker recognize `failure_class == 'opt_in_required'` (or an `isinstance(exc, AgyOptInRequiredError)`) as a walkable skip that advances to the next hop without counting as a failed voice, or (b) resolve the gate at chain-build time (cheval's chain resolver drops gemini-headless hops when agy_opt_in_enabled() is False) so the adapter refusal is only a defense-in-depth backstop. Add a test that walks a [gemini-headless, gemini-api] chain with the gate off and asserts the HTTP hop answers.

findings.cross_file_justification: resolve_effort (diff) returns the source value 'extra'; cmd_invoke (diff, cheval.py:2834-2835) forwards it unconditionally as MODELINV effort_source; modelinv.py (diff, line 498) and the cheval.py comment both document the field's domain as `caller | catalog | none`, and the MODELINV payload schema (model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json, in this diff but truncated) is the enforced contract for that field.
findings.description: resolve_effort has four rungs and returns `'extra'` as the source for a CLI entry whose legacy `extra.effort` / `extra.reasoning_effort` supplied the value. Every downstream description of `effort_source` in this diff (the modelinv.py parameter comment at line 498, the cmd_invoke emit comment at line 2834, the docstring in emit_model_invoke_complete) lists the domain as `caller | catalog | none` and omits `extra`. If the payload schema enum matches those comments, every invocation that lands on a headless entry carrying `extra.effort` (the stock claude-headless entries do) emits a model_invoke_complete event that fails schema validation; if the schema was widened, the three comments are wrong and the dry-run label map (cheval.py:1543) is the only place that knows about `extra`.
findings.failure_mode: A CLI-entry invoke with legacy extra.effort writes `effort_source: "extra"` into .run/model-invoke.jsonl; trajectory/schema validators reject the event or downstream readers keyed on the documented three-value enum misclassify it.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one domain. Either add `extra` to the schema enum and every comment/docstring, or collapse the legacy rung into `catalog` (it is still a catalog-sourced value) and keep the three-value contract. Add a test in test_effort_catalog_default.py that validates an emitted payload with `effort_source` from each rung against the schema.

findings.description: validate_config() now appends an error whenever the opt-in is off. Since off is the default and gemini-headless is in the stock catalog, every default install reports a provider configuration error. An opt-in that is deliberately off is not a misconfiguration; any whole-catalog validation path (cheval validate, run-preflight.sh, loa-status) that treats a non-empty error list as failure will fail or warn on a pristine install.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight/validate tooling flags a default install as misconfigured, training operators to ignore validation output or to opt in just to silence it.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the gated state as an informational/skip entry (or return [] with a logger.info) rather than an error; reserve errors for an opted-in route whose binary or cli_model is missing. If a consumer needs to know the route is off, expose it via a separate `is_enabled()` seam.

findings.description: agy_opt_in_enabled() walks the cwd for a project root and re-parses the full system defaults catalog plus .loa.config.yaml on every call. It is called at the top of complete(), health_check() and validate_config(), so each dispatch and each health probe pays a full YAML parse of the ~500-line catalog. It also resolves the root via the cwd walk rather than the root cheval already loaded, so a cheval process invoked from a non-project cwd silently reads 'off' even if the operator opted in at the real project root. The broad `except Exception` also swallows a malformed config as 'off' with no log line, so an operator who typo'd the YAML gets a refusal that blames the missing key.
findings.failure_mode: Repeated parse cost per hop and per health check; a cwd mismatch or YAML typo quietly disables an opted-in route with a misleading 'set agy_opt_in: true' message.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache per (root, mtime) or resolve once at adapter construction / cheval startup and pass the boolean in; log at WARNING inside the except so a parse failure is distinguishable from an absent key.

findings.description: The 'sets both params.default_effort and extra.effort' WARN fires for any entry, including HTTP entries, whose extra.effort is by the function's own docstring never read ('HTTP entries never read it'). It also fires when an explicit --effort was passed and neither catalog rung is consulted. The message tells the operator to 'drop one' for a conflict that has no effect on that entry.
findings.failure_mode: Spurious one-per-process WARN on HTTP entries carrying a vestigial extra.effort, noise in operator logs.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the 'both' warning on `_is_cli_entry(entry)` (the only case where extra.effort would otherwise have been read) and skip it when `explicit` is set.

findings.description: _effort_on_wire returns the requested effort unchanged for any entry `_is_cli_entry` matches (kind == cli or auth_type == headless). Only the claude-headless adapter passes `--effort` through; codex, grok, gemini/agy and cursor headless adapters build fixed argv with no effort flag. So `effort_effective` in MODELINV and dry-run claims an effort reached the wire on hops where nothing was sent, which is the opposite of the field's stated purpose (the value the answering hop actually put on the wire).
findings.failure_mode: Telemetry overstates effort application for non-claude CLI hops; a later audit of 'effort honored' is wrong for those providers.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the pass-through to entries whose provider type is claude-headless (or ask the adapter class via a `supports_effort` attribute), returning None for the others.

findings.description: For a measured entry the test sets `cap = entry['effective_input_ceiling']`, so `expected = min(effective_input_ceiling, context_window - default_max_tokens)` and the subsequent equality assert is a tautology whenever the I2 invariant holds (which the next line already asserts independently). The 'computed, not a constant' property is no longer checked for calibrated entries at all; the only remaining content is the I2 bound. Combined with the catalog's claude-opus-5-5 entry being written as `operator_set` 936000 with `sample_size: null` from a probe whose recorded outcome was partial (the tool itself writes only on `clean`), the suite no longer has any check that the calibrated value is derived from a recorded measurement.
findings.failure_mode: A hand-edited or mis-clamped calibrated ceiling (e.g. one exceeding ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens) passes the floor suite unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: For measured entries assert `effective_input_ceiling == min(cal['measured_input_tokens'], context_window - default_max_tokens(entry))` and `probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling`, which ties the catalog value to the recorded measurement rather than to itself.
